objection.status: error reported by an ordinary grader
objection.quote:
Thus $V$ contains **at most one** positive number.  Consequently, either  

* (i) $g\equiv 0$ (constant), which gives $f(x)=x$, a solution; or  
* (ii) there is $c>0$ such that $V \subseteq \{0, c\}$ with both values attainable.
objection.witness: The classification jumps from 'V contains at most one positive number' to 'V ⊆ {0} or V ⊆ {0,c}', without ruling out g(x)<0 for some x. This case is never treated, so the case analysis (and Lemma 1, which assumes b∈{0,c}) is incomplete. (Repairable in two lines: if g(x₀)=-d<0, iterating (4) gives g(x₀-nd)=-d and x₀-nd>0 for all n, impossible.)
